title: Lifecycle helper — mandatory-failure matrix
summary: Every mandatory failure mode of the lifecycle helper returns nonzero. The matrix below was exercised directly against packaging/lifecycle.sh with fake roots (--root <DESTDIR>) and a fake namtor-pam-edit stub. Each failure produces a FATAL line on stderr and a receipt with status=failed. No mandatory failure is swallowed.

matrix.actual: nonzero (FATAL: no ONNX models / model <id> missing onnx)

matrix.defect: tampered model — onnx sha256 does not match the manifest variant

non_mandatory_best_effort.behaviour: WARN and skip the PAM subprocess call; the phase still validates non-PAM state and exits 0 if all mandatory checks pass. Rationale: PAM may legitimately not be configured yet on a fresh system, and the helper must not fail an install because a optional integration tool is missing.

non_mandatory_best_effort.item: systemctl / systemd-sysusers / systemd-tmpfiles absent or fake-root
non_mandatory_best_effort.behaviour: Skipped silently on fake roots (--root != /); best-effort `|| true` on real roots. Runtime dir creation is validated by check_dir regardless.
Best-effort, skipped on fake roots. Not a mandatory gate.

WARN and continue (`|| true`). A failed PAM snapshot must not block an upgrade; a failed disable-all must not block removal (PAM may already be disabled). The task spec lists missing model/sysuser/service as the mandatory failures, not PAM-subprocess failures.

invariants_asserted.never_edit_pam_on_install: PASS — pre-install and post-install phase bodies contain no pam-edit enable/disable/migrate/snapshot/purge and no /etc/pam.d write
invariants_asserted.never_call_nonexistent_cli: PASS — no `models ensure` or `namtor-cli models` reference in lifecycle.sh
invariants_asserted.no_pam_default_target: PASS — no gdm-password/system-auth/password-auth/common-auth hardcoded as a default
invariants_asserted.idempotent: PASS — post-install twice → same exit code + same receipt (modulo timestamp)
invariants_asserted.fake_root_testable: PASS — every operation rebased under --root; no real-filesystem writes when --root is set
